# The developer's hand

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

What a product builder meets that no golden shows.

- **Rule 41's ceiling** — every component schema carries an example; the count without one only falls — a declared example lowers it, and you commit the printed LOWER line (`quality/rules.yaml:5812`)
- **Derived files** — `scope.PRODUCT_DERIVED` names what a product commits but never hand-writes: migrations, `max_migration.txt`, `<noun>_authz_baseline.json`, the published document and its client (the `rules.yaml` prose says `authz_baseline.json`; the glob is `*authz_baseline.json`) (`quality/djb/scope.py:2067`)
- **`scaffold --check` on a copy** — diffs your copy against its own fences — a copy is checked against its golden, never the template's (`apps/core/management/commands/scaffold.py:66`)
- **Rule 42 reads one hop** — a service is reached when a door calls it, or one credited hop through the app's `services/` package — not every reader (`quality/rules.yaml:6541`)
- **`Integration*` is not in the SDK** — the integrations census is the engine's (`pilecap/_internal.py`), so no `Integration*` name is exported; an inbound handler lives in your `integrations.py` (`pilecap/_internal.py:28`)
- **A signed door takes no bearer** — a route whose signature is its credential is declared with `pilecap.declare_signed_door` from your `apps.py` `ready()` and must be on rule 3's allow-list; a bearer, `X-Tenant` or `X-Org` sent to it gets your refusal (`apps/core/middleware.py:582`)
- **Adopt by hand owes parity** — `scaffold adopt` writes the verb's door-parity rows and census addend; a hand adopt must write the same or rule 46 reds (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:997`)
- **Adopt floors** — `scaffold` measures rule 91 over what a copy wrote and prints each new tail as a line to delete; it records no floor (`inflow: refused`) (`apps/core/scaffold/floors.py:66`)
- **Reserved nouns** — a noun whose copy would serve a name a canary plant carries is refused, the plant named; `Gadget` is one — see the list below (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:976`)
- **`adopt` vs `verb`** — `scaffold adopt <verb>` copies a WHOLE noun into a fresh `newapp`; on a noun already scaffolded, `scaffold verb <app> <Noun> <verb>` adds a plain verb (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:933`)
- **`roads` without the worked example** — a product that deleted `apps/example*` gets one `worked example removed` line, exit 0 (`apps/core/management/commands/roads.py:63`)
- **The noun's authz baseline** — `scaffold noun` writes `apps/<app>/tests/<noun>_authz_baseline.json` on its first run — commit it; `DJB_BASELINE_WRITE=1` is only for a noun built by hand that lacks one (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:783`)
- **The noun's owner** — `scaffold noun` copies Widget's `owner = ForeignKey(AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=CASCADE)` and `Lifecycle(kind=BOUNDED)`: the noun's rows die with the person who owns them, and that is the noun's declared death (house rule 31: every model declares how its data dies). Rows that must outlive their owner change both in one commit — `on_delete=PROTECT` (the person cannot be deleted while they own rows) or `SET_NULL` with `null=True`, and the `lifecycle` that now says how the rows do die — then `./scripts/feature.sh <app>` makes the migration (`apps/core/scaffold/goldens/noun/models.py-tpl:25`)
- **One noun per app** — `scaffold noun` writes whole modules and never overwrites one, so an app holds one noun; a second noun is a second `newapp` (its children come by `scaffold child`) (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:1120`)
- **App labels** — a lowercase Python identifier and plural (house rule 16), named for the collection its noun belongs to and never the noun's own plural — `workorders` holds `Job`, and house rule 32 refuses `jobs` because the copy would mount at `/jobs/`, an app label; `apps.<label>` is every module's import path; a deliberate singular (a mass noun such as `billing`), a module outside rule 11's canonical names or a view rule 3 admits open is an entry a product adds under `scope_extensions: {16: …}` (or `{11: …}`, `{3: …}`) in `quality/local/rules.yaml`, with its reason (`apps/core/management/commands/newapp.py:168`)
- **Service verbs** — a service opens with a word of house rule 16's lexicon (`service_verbs` in `quality/rules.yaml`) or of the product's own under `service_verbs:` in `quality/local/rules.yaml`; `roads shape verb` reads the same union, and a word the template already declares is exit 2 naming it (`quality/engine/lexicon.py:45`)
- **Shapes go on nouns** — `docs/sdk/shapes.md` lists each shape's arguments and what it goes on; a shape `on noun` is refused on a child row (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:688`)
- **A verb that is a status step** — `scaffold verb <app> <Noun> <verb> --transition <from>-><to>` writes the verb as one step of the noun's enum (`transition_<noun>`, `409 conflict` from any other value), never a `touch` copy patched by hand (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/verb.py:210`)
- **Filter lookups are closed** — `scaffold filter` takes a declared lookup only; an undeclared one is a named refusal (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/filter.py:22`)
- **A product's rule ids** — `manage.py declare <ns>` writes `rule_id_namespace:` and `template_rule_ids_through:` into `quality/local/rules.yaml` — one without the other is `--fast` exit 2; [day zero](day-zero.md) is the order (`apps/core/management/commands/declare.py:34`)
- **`template_only` on your gate** — a platform test wearing `@pytest.mark.template_only` asserts the template's own tree; on yours it is skipped (`apps/`) or deselected (`quality/tests`), printing `template-only: this tree declares rule_id_namespace <yours>; <why>` — expected, not a red (`apps/testing/template_only.py:45`)
- **The conventions** — `django-conventions` is the template builders' long form; this reference cites it where a rule binds (`.claude/skills/django-conventions/SKILL.md:15`)
- **A verb that sends a message** — see [Sending a message](sending-messages.md) — `pilecap.comms.send` inside the service's transaction, never a mailer of your own (`apps/comms/services.py:715`)

Nouns whose url names a canary plant serves — `scaffold` is refused for them:

`allow`, `bauble`, `canary_bin`, `canary_card`, `canary_crate`, `canary_hamper`, `canary_shelf`, `canary_tote`, `canary_trolley`, `cog`, `doodad`, `doohickey`, `gadget`, `gimcrack`, `gizmo`, `gizmo_bin`, `gizmo_cart`, `gizmo_shelf`, `gizmo_stencil`, `gubbins`, `knickknack`, `nicknack`, `oddment`, `thingummy`, `trinket`, `whatnot`, `widget`, `widget_canary_added`, `widget_canary_bullet`, `widget_canary_probe`, `widget_canary_probes`, `widget_negative_bullet`, `widget_negative_probe`, `widget_silent_probe`, `zzz_canary_borrowed`, `zzz_canary_field_note`, `zzz_canary_gadget`, `zzz_canary_headed`, `zzz_canary_notebook`, `zzz_canary_noted`, `zzz_canary_shadow`, `zzz_canary_thing`

Names a canary plant serves as `list_<x>` (a copy may not serve them):

`list_connections`, `list_doodads`, `list_gadgets`, `list_gizmos`
